title: How Personal Rapid Transport Works
summary: Josh Clark and Chris Pallette discuss personal rapid transit (PRT), a small-car, automated, grade-separated rail taxi-like system. They cover its 1950s American origins, claimed lower build cost than light rail (about $16 million per mile versus about $40 million for light rail, with a Heathrow Airport installation cited), safety and reliability concerns such as a failed car stopping the whole line, a Simpsons "Marge vs. the Monorail" reference as a criticism, and installations planned in Sweden and Abu Dhabi, including Masdar City aiming to be a zero-carbon city. Opening and closing segments include chatter about Chris shaving his goatee and on-air ad reads for the sponsors and the camera promo.

segments.title: Opening banter and sponsor read
segments.summary: Josh introduces the episode and guest writer Chris Pallette, with banter about Chris shaving his goatee. A sponsor read and camera promo are included.

segments.title: What personal rapid transit is
segments.summary: Josh and Chris introduce personal rapid transit (PRT) as a idea with roots in 1950s American urban design, combining features of subways and taxis, with small cars on a rail line that riders don't share.

segments.title: Cost compared with light rail
segments.summary: The hosts say PRT is cheaper to build than light rail, citing about $16 million per mile of track versus about $40 million for light rail, and a system being built at Heathrow Airport. Chris explains that light rail needs larger cars and wider track.

segments.title: Criticisms and the Simpsons monorail
segments.summary: Opponents question PRT's reliability, since a failed car could stop the cars behind it on a shared track. The hosts also discuss a Simpsons monorail episode as a satirical take on the system.

segments.title: PRT in Sweden and Abu Dhabi
segments.summary: The hosts note PRT systems being installed in Sweden and Abu Dhabi, and describe Masdar City, a development outside Abu Dhabi aiming to be the first zero carbon footprint city, which includes a planned PRT system.

segments.title: Closing and sponsor read
segments.summary: Josh points listeners to the related article on HowStuffWorks and invites feedback by email, followed by a repeated sponsor read.
